romans.4.p1.b1.text: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?

romans.4.p1.b2.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

romans.4.p1.b3.text: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

romans.4.p1.b4.text: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.

romans.4.p2.b1.text: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

romans.4.p2.b2.text: Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

romans.4.p2.b3.text: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”

romans.4.p3.b1.text: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? …

romans.4.p3.b2.text: … It was not after, but before.

romans.4.p3.b3.text: … So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

romans.4.p3.b4.text: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.

romans.4.p4.b1.text: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

romans.4.p4.b2.text: … so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham.

romans.4.p4.b3.text: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” …

romans.4.p5.b1.text: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”

romans.4.p5.b2.text: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.

romans.4.p5.b3.text: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.

romans.4.p5.b4.text: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”

romans.4.p6.b1.text: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,

romans.4.p6.b2.text: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

romans.4.p6.b3.text: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.
